rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to spend follows the command to act rightly: spending from good earnings affirms faith, and purifying one's gift has the broader benefit.
rows.anchor: ولما رغب في الفعل وتخليصه عن الشوائب أتبعه المال المنفق منه فأمر بطيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade profits and produce are both blessings created from the earth; this should encourage generous giving of the best lawful goods and deter miserliness or giving illicit goods.
rows.anchor: كل ما يتقلب العباد فيه من أنفسهم وغيرها نعمة منه أنشأها من الأرض

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The address to those earning through their labor suggests the Emigrants, followed by those giving from crops and cultivation, suggesting the Helpers.
rows.anchor: قدم خطاب المكتسبين بأعمالهم كأنهم المهاجرون وعطف عليهم المنفقين من الحرث والزرع كأنهم الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyammamu means deliberately undertaking to target the bad portion for giving.
rows.anchor: أي لا تتكلفوا أن تقصدوا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Khabith is an intensive form: what the soul finds repellent outwardly and inwardly, opposite the good that it welcomes.
rows.anchor: الخبيث صيغة مبالغة بزيادة الياء من الخبث وهو ما ينافر حس النفس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The construction implies giving only the bad, extending the prohibition even to one who gives both good and bad but does not single out the bad.
rows.anchor: ففي إلاحته معنى حصر كأنهم لا ينفقون إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test is whether a giver would accept the inferior property from someone who owed him; one would take it only by overlooking its defect reluctantly.
rows.anchor: أي إذا كان لكم على أحد حق فأعطاكموه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Ighmad is to avert one's gaze from a defect; its root evokes a sleep that veils the senses and then clears.
rows.anchor: من الإغماض وهو الإغضاء عن العيب فيما يستعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wholly perfect and rich: He needs neither poor-quality gifts nor spending itself; the command is kindness to people, for reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: وليست به حاجة تدعوه إلى أخذ الرديء ولا رغبكم في أصل الإنفاق لحاجة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards a good giver abundantly; He has always been and remains praiseworthy, whether His decree accords with human preference or not.
rows.anchor: يجازي المحسن أفضل الجزاء على أنه لم يزل محمودا ولا يزال

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Hamid is an intensive form from praise, which is God's even, unvarying order whether it pleases human souls or opposes them.
rows.anchor: صيغة مبالغة بزيادة ياء من الحمد الذي هو سواء أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about Satan counters the question why people are usually miserly after hearing God's true promise: the enemy promises the opposite and lies.
rows.anchor: أتبعه بما للعدو الكاذب من ضد ذلك فقال محذرا من البخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's name evokes ruin and distance; either trait alone warrants avoiding him, and their combination makes avoidance still more urgent.
rows.anchor: فإنه يقتضي الهلاك والبعد , وأحد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Fear of poverty drives worldly people to sever ties, withdraw, hoard, and remain poor; even the owner of the world is poor if greedy, while the content are rich.
rows.anchor: كل حريص فقير ولو ملك الدنيا

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: A servant of the Rich should know he is enriched by his Master; fearing poverty is the servant's flight from his Lord, and poverty is lacking what one needs when needed.
rows.anchor: ففي خوف الفقر إباق العبد عن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's command to indecency undermines charity through reminders, injury, and other appetites, potentially destroying property and lives.
rows.anchor: المبطلة له من المن والأذى وغيرهما من مستلذات الأنفس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Fahsha covers everything jointly condemned by reason, religious law, and nature; here its chief referent is miserliness, the gravest disease and root of worldly and next-worldly evil.
rows.anchor: وأعظم مراد بها هنا البخل الذي هو أدوأ داء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness for human shortcomings and increased bounty in both worlds; every blessing is a gift of His grace.
rows.anchor: لما وقع منكم من تقصير

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Calling God expansive and knowing weakens Satan's scheme and promises the person tempted by fear of poverty and indecency that God knows human weakness and susceptibility to whispers.
rows.anchor: وفي إشعاره توهين لكيد الشيطان ووعد كريم للمفتون بخوف الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final parable passage closes with encouragement and warning, as the opening of the parables did.
rows.anchor: فختم آخر آيات الأمثال بما ختم به أولها ترغيبا وترهيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those praised are elevated among the righteous; the context implies that most others do not possess these qualities, and one who lacks uprightness is fit for nothing.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن من لم يستقم لم يصلح لشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever good people do, including spending, is preserved and thanked rather than denied; the passive wording is chosen reverently.
rows.anchor: بل هو مشكور لكم بسبب فعلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the God-fearing whose piety prompts every good deed, rewarding them greatly; He also knows and punishes others as He wills.
rows.anchor: من الفاعلين الذين كانت التقوى حاملة لهم على كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the address reading the syntax is as explained; the third-person reading also fits its surrounding construction.
rows.anchor: قراءة الغيبة فأمرها واضح في نظمها بما قلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Israelite example exposed their false claim to Abraham's religion, the passage warns of those who prefer wealth, authority, and worldly status over faith.
rows.anchor: على وجه أنتج أن بنيه كاذون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This general statement applies to all disbelievers, including those who claim faith hypocritically: their wealth and children cannot avert anything from God.
rows.anchor: على وجه يعم جميع الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers are confined to Hell forever; this follows from the conclusion that their assets and offspring cannot save them.
rows.anchor: ثم استأنف ما يفيد ملازمتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their spending, whether meant as worship or not, bears no fruit because they omitted sincerity, the condition by which it is accepted.
rows.anchor: لكونهم ضيعوا الوجه الذي به يقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The icy, destructive wind striking a field owned by people who wronged themselves through unbelief images their wasted spending and wealth, bringing toil and harm in both worlds.
rows.anchor: أي بالبناء على غير أساس الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison has two paired images: wind destroying the crop images spending's harm, while the ruined crop images wealth that yields no return beyond loss and effort.
rows.anchor: ومثل إنفاقهم له في كونه ضرهم ولم ينفعهم مثل الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy uses sensible wind damage to depict hidden, abstract wasted spending, and visible crop ruin to depict the intelligible loss of wealth after toil.
rows.anchor: جعلت في إهلاكها مثلا لضياع إنفاقهم الذي هو أمر معنوي خفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by implication: the likeness of spending is omitted first because the wind supplies it, and the field is omitted second because spending supplies it.
rows.anchor: حذف أولا مثل الإنفاق لدلالة الريح عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not wrong either group: disbelievers spent outside His prescribed way, while field owners failed to protect their crops through obedience; the verse suggests obedience can protect crops from calamity.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على أن أهل الطاعات تحرس ضوائعهم من الآفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' self-wrong remains their own even if their spending seems to spite believers: believers ultimately prevail, making that injury void and an added punishment for the spenders.
rows.anchor: وأن ظلمهم مقصور على أنفسهم

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads the warning as addressed to the Prophet; the other readers make those who withhold the grammatical subject.
rows.anchor: وعند الباقين الفاعل الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The withheld wealth consists of religious dues from God's grace, not something its possessors earned through miserliness.
rows.anchor: لأنه ثمرة كونه من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They wrongly suppose hoarding will grow their wealth; miserliness is harmful, and what they withheld will become a terrifying serpent encircling their necks and striking their faces on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: يجعل لهم بوعد صادق لا خلف فيه بعد الإملاء لهم طوقا بأن يجعله شجاعا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet said that one given wealth who fails to pay its zakat will have that wealth become a bald serpent with two black marks, which collars and seizes him, saying it is his wealth and hoard; he then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: من آتاه الله مالا فلم يؤد زكاته مثل له ماله شجاعا أقرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since owners spend when they know wealth will pass to an heir, God explains that all wealth belongs to Him and that He will inherit the heavens and earth after reviving beings and ending their transient possessions.
rows.anchor: فلله كل ما في أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the passage concerns hidden acts and unseen matters, ending with God's knowledge of people's deeds gives a forceful warning; the wording addresses the followers in most readings.
rows.anchor: صرف الخطاب إلى الأتباع في قراءة غير ابن كثير وأبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address reading is more threatening than retaining the preceding third-person construction, and fronting the phrase about their deeds stresses God's knowledge beyond human comprehension.
rows.anchor: وهو أبلغ في الوعيد من تركه على مقتضى السياق من الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's being informed encompasses every act of the heart, tongue, and limbs.
rows.anchor: العمل شاملا لتصرفات الجوارح كلها من القلب واللسان وسائر الأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers are Jews who claim that God's request for a loan proves He is poor and they are rich; this resumes the theme of the People of the Book's hostility, envy, and effort to sow doubt.
rows.anchor: وهذا رجوع منه سبحانه وتعالى إلى إتمام ما نبه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to record their words may use the future particle for emphasis, or in its usual sense of delay, giving them time to repent before their testimony is sealed; fuller discussion comes in al-Zukhruf.
rows.anchor: على بابها من المهلة للحث على التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their killing of prophets is a further, graver aggression: the possessive construction and broken plural imply numerous killings and entrenched rebellion, while without right leaves no possible excuse.
rows.anchor: فهو أعظم ذما مما قبله من التعبير بالفعل المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the heavens and earth, including every possible refuge, and fully encompasses all things; His power leaves no escape from what He wills.
rows.anchor: والحال أن ملكه محيط بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on creation serves the surah's chief aim of monotheism and faith, which saves from punishment; the Qur'an enlightens hearts, and submission to the Abrahamic way depends on the Prophet's truthfulness.
rows.anchor: دل على ذلك بالتنبيه على التفكر فيه الموجب للتوحيد الذي هو المقصد الأعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah begins by establishing the Prophet's truth through the Qur'an's inimitability in meaning and form, refuting doubts, and exposing the People of the Book; it now turns to signs of knowledge.
rows.anchor: من الترغيب والترهيب شرع في بث أنوا المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vast, beneficial heavens and earth and the orderly alternation of night and day point to a changer and to the messengers' teachings, since their ordered course requires the decree of the Almighty, All-Knowing.
rows.anchor: على منهاج قويم وسير لا يكون إلا بتقدير العزيز العليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with the corresponding verse in al-Baqara, which presents eight kinds of proof, this passage offers three: beginners need many proofs, while the spiritually illuminated can be distracted by excess.
rows.anchor: في أخت هذه الآية في سورة البقرة ثمانية أنواع من الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage focuses on the heavens because their scale and wonders are more overpowering and lead the heart more quickly to God's grandeur; al-Baqara closes with reason, while this passage addresses those with insight beyond satanic whispers and illusion.
rows.anchor: وانتقال القلب منها إلى عظمته سبحانه وتعالى وكبريائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may all claim peak discernment, so the passage identifies those who truly merit that description by their remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: كل مميز يدعي أنه في الذروة من الرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God while standing, sitting, and lying down covers work, rest, and sleep and expresses continuous vigilance, rather than merely frequent remembrance.
rows.anchor: في اشتغالهم بأشغالهم وفي وقت استراحتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge comes from signs in the horizons and within people; cosmic signs are greater, as 40:57 states that creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating humanity.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت آيات المعرفة إما في الآفاق وإما في الأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Contemplating the immense heavens, earth, benefits, and creatures teaches that another abode must establish truth and justice, remove falsehood and oppression, and distinguish wrongdoers from the righteous.
rows.anchor: مع جري ما فيهما من الحيوان الذي خلقا لأجله على غير انتظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer that creation was not made in vain means this transient world is not the sole purpose, since justice is not fully rendered here and another abode must bring judgment.
rows.anchor: بل إنما خلقته لأجل دار أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying Subhanaka frees God from the apparent defect of a world where evil prevails; beginning supplication with praise teaches proper etiquette, and greater knowledge increases fear and pleading.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك تعليم العباد أدب الدعاء بتقديم الثناء قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God may rightly do anything, including punish the obedient, seeking refuge from that punishment is meaningful only after affirming His freedom from defect.
rows.anchor: فإنه يحسن منه كل شيء من تعذيب الطائع وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognizing a just afterlife, the supplicants ask to be spared its punishment and the Fire.
rows.anchor: رغبة في الخلاص في تلك الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea combines the punishment mentioned at the end of the previous phrase with the Fire warned of in 3:185.
rows.anchor: والنار المحذر منها في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to unite people in monotheism taught by Al Imran and in the Book urged by al-Baqara, for the religion gathered by al-Fatiha, warning against division promoted by Shas ibn Qays and his like.
rows.anchor: الاجتماع على التوحيد الذي هدت إليه آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah is among the last revealed.
rows.anchor: من أواخر ما نزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhari's virtues-of-the-Qur'an section recounts that an Iraqi asked Aisha for her codex to arrange the Qur'an, since people recited it out of order.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في فضائل القرآ

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha explained that early revelation emphasized Paradise and Hell; after people embraced Islam, lawful and unlawful rulings came, since commands to abandon wine or adultery at the outset would have been rejected.
rows.anchor: إنما نزل أول ما نزل منه سورة من المفصل

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha said Muhammad received revelation at Mecca while she was a young girl playing; al-Baqara and al-Nisa were revealed only after she joined him, and she dictated the surah's verses from her codex.
rows.anchor: وما نزلت سورة البقرة والنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha's point is that the Qur'an reaches the highest eloquence by descending in a way suited to changing circumstances, then arranging discourse to suit the audience's understanding.
rows.anchor: القرآن حاز أعلى البلاغة في إنزاله مطابقا لما تقتضيه الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of accepted repentance is expressed with a preposition of obligation, encouraging repentance and making God's acceptance a sure promise.
rows.anchor: عبر بحرف الاستعلاء المؤذن بالوجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suw' includes any sin, whether disobedience or unbelief; doing it in ignorance underscores sin's ugliness, especially adultery by an old man.
rows.anchor: سوء كان من فسق أو كفر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar reports from Salman, with a good chain according to the author, that three will not enter Paradise: an old adulterer, a lying ruler, and an arrogant poor man.
rows.anchor: رواه البزار بإسناد جيد عن سلمان رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Muslim and others report from Abu Hurayra that God will neither speak to, look at, nor purify three on Judgment Day, who face painful punishment: an old adulterer, lying king, and arrogant poor man; many Companions report it by many routes.
rows.anchor: وهو في مسلم وغيره عن أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The old person's approaching death and weakened bodily powers should extinguish sexual desire and the impulse of ignorance, unlike the stronger drives of youth.
rows.anchor: حضور الموت بالقوة القريبة من الفعل وإضعاف القوى الموهنة لداعية الشهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows either sense of jahalah: opposite forbearance or opposite knowledge.
rows.anchor: إن المراد بالجهالة ضد الحلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
rows.claim: Citing al-Qazzaz, Abd al-Haqq explains that jahiliya refers to idolaters and derives from wind making a branch sway; ignorance is movement away from truth and knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله - يعني القزاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus sinning in folly, agitation, or lightness is like acting without knowledge and resembles the conduct of people of the pre-Islamic age.
rows.anchor: يعملون السوء ملتبسين بسفه أو بحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance may be renewed after sin; the phrase min qareeb refers to some time within one's remaining lifespan, before persisting until death.
rows.anchor: كناية عن عدم الإصرار إلى الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The use of thumma signals that repentance may be distant and difficult after entanglement in sin, especially when someone has repeatedly fallen into it.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى بعد التوبة ولا سيما مع القرب ممن واقع المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent sincerely are elevated and restored to their former closeness to God; He knows their sincerity and intentions and acts with perfect wisdom.
rows.anchor: يردهم إلى ما كانوا فيه عندهم من مكانة القرب قبل مواقعة الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is not accepted from persistent sinners who do not return soon and wait until death reaches the throat; foregrounding the person facing death creates suspense and fear.
rows.anchor: على وجه يجوز كل سامع وقوعه عليه - أهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dying sinner's claim to repent now may be spoken aloud, as Pharaoh did, or held in the heart; the verse sharply urges haste.
rows.anchor: أي بلسانه كفرعون , أو قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same ruling covers those who die as unbelievers, literally or figuratively, without repenting, including at the death-rattle.
rows.anchor: حقيقة أو مجازا , من غير أن يتوبوا , ولا عند الغرغرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse groups persistent sin and unbelief to deter sinning, because withdrawal from sin becomes difficult after committing it; both face painful punishment, while unrepentant believers remain subject to God's will.
rows.anchor: فسوى بين الفسق والكفر تنفيرا من الفسق لصعوبة النزع عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is delivered through revelation and is not restricted to the fearful; it exposes the disbelievers' dullness in denying what anyone should reasonably fear.
rows.anchor: بل الإشارة إلى جلافتهم وعظيم بلادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering is against people's will, to their Lord who created and nurtured them despite their inadequate gratitude.
rows.anchor: المحسن إليهم بالإيجاد والتربية مع التقصير في الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will have no protector to rescue them by force and no intercessor to rescue them through rank or effective advocacy; all beings are beneath God's dominion.
rows.anchor: يتولى أمورهم فينقذهم قهرا مما يخافون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La'allahum yattaqun means their condition may become that of people who hope to place a safeguard between themselves and God's punishment.
rows.anchor: ليكون حالهم حال من يرجى أن يجعل بينه وبين عذاب الله وقاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those the Prophet must not drive away are poor Muslims, devoted to their Lord in contrast to unbelievers who call on powerless beings.
rows.anchor: عكس ما عليه الكفار في دعاء من لا يملك لهم ضرا ولا نفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening may mean both ends of each day, the two daily prayers, or continuous worship; their long constancy indicates sincerity rather than ostentation.
rows.anchor: في طرفي النهار مطلقا أو بصلاتيهما أو يكون كناية عن الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy polytheists promised to follow Muhammad if he expelled his humble companions, whom they disparaged as insincere and driven by need.
rows.anchor: وعدوه صلى الله عليه وسلم الاتباع إن طرد من تبعه ممن يأنفون من مجالستهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet has no stake in worldly gain from expelling the poor or accepting the rich; his mission calls people away from worldly life.
rows.anchor: التي هو مبعوث للتنفير عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of responsibility for one another's account means the Prophet sees only outward conduct; he need not expel them over a fear that they are insincere or that they burden him.
rows.anchor: ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading of the denial of mutual accounting, linked to 18:28, concerns provision: the Prophet's invitation is for the afterlife, and neither the poor nor the Prophet depends on the other's provision.
rows.anchor: يعني أن دعاءك إلى الله إنما مداره الأمر الأخروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adduces lexicons and usage showing that hisab can mean sufficiency or provision: 78:36 gives an abundant gift; the verb can mean feeding to satisfaction; and a report from Simak says hosts did not honor their guest.
rows.anchor: صاحب القاموس وغيره : الحساب : الكافي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد الهروي
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd explains ahsabtuhu as giving someone enough until he says, “That suffices me.”
rows.anchor: أي أعطيته الكفاية حتى قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “without account” in 2:212 means without stinting or constriction; Ibn Faris likewise glosses ahsabtuhu as giving enough or what satisfies.
rows.anchor: بغير تقتير وتضييق , وفي حديث سماك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expelling the poor would be unjustly putting things out of place and would not make the wealthy polytheists believe; guidance belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: وليس هدايتهم إلا إلينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested groups through the Prophet's appointment and through differences of faith, wealth, and poverty; elites scorned the poor as unworthy of God's favor.
rows.anchor: بالتخصيص بالإيمان والغنى والفقر ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elite's objection anticipates their later demand to receive what God's messengers received; God alone knows who merits preference through gratitude.
rows.anchor: فالآية ناظرة إلى ما يأتي في هذه السورة من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection fails because only God knows who deserves to be favored for gratitude, unlike the elite who reject the grateful poor.
rows.anchor: الذين يستحقون أن يفضلوا لشكرهم على غيرهم لكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding commands to measure fairly and the promise of exact recompense establish the divine capacity for perfect weighing; the previous verse's encompassing knowledge reinforces that point.
rows.anchor: أكد الأمر أيضا وقصره على علمه هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing may be of the records, the deeds after they are embodied in fitting forms, or another manner; God may simply give hearts knowledge of it.
rows.anchor: صحف الأعمال أو للأعمال أنفسها بعد تصويرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perhaps the weighing is attached to God's “We” in the preceding verse: He does not merely recount deeds but weighs them so everyone sees their exact equality.
rows.anchor: إنا لا نكتفي بما نقص بل نزنه فيصير بحيث يظهر لكل أحد

rows.speaker: أبو حيان وعلي بن الحسن النحوي الأصفهاني
rows.claim: They parse al-wazn as subject, yawma'idhin as its adverb, and al-haqq as predicate; al-Asbahani further objects that a definite verbal noun rarely governs, though 4:148 is an example.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان وعلي بن الحسن النحوي الأصفهاني في إعرابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weighing is confined to truth: what occurs exactly matches it, with no excess or departure from the measure.
rows.anchor: في ذلك اليوم مقصور على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah urges following the Book and Messenger, establishes monotheism and resurrection through creation and past nations' destruction, and warns that rejection brings worldly and final punishment.
rows.anchor: الحث على اتباع الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy scales sink as familiar weights do; each deed is weighed separately, urging people to improve every deed.
rows.anchor: عبر بها عنها إشارة إلى أن كل عمل يوزن على حدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with heavy scales are successful, attaining all their aims.
rows.anchor: ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the scale holding good deeds should naturally grow heavy, while the scale holding sins should grow light.
rows.anchor: وحق الميزان توضع فيه الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales are light lose their own selves, their chief capital, through persistently putting God's signs in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: التي هي رأس مالهم فكيف بما دونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds people that He empowered them, gave them strength and abundant favor, and made every place on earth usable, even for reflection.
rows.anchor: مكناكم من إنجائها بخلق القوى والقدر وإدرار النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'ayish means all things by which one lives; living itself is spending one's days in beneficial activity, and the y in the word is original rather than a glide.
rows.anchor: وهي أشياء يحصل بها العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People enjoy the earth's provisions and the powers God created but worship others, so they give little thanks.
rows.anchor: أوجدهم وقواهم وخلق لهم ما يديم قواهم فأكلوا خيره وعبدوا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This unusually clear exposition details rulings and distinguishes confused matters for people capable of learning, so they can reach sound belief and righteous action.
rows.anchor: هذا التفصيل فائق فهل يفصل غيره هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, the Benefactor who gave the best religion, forbids every indecency, public or hidden, as well as sin generally.
rows.anchor: وهي ما زاد قبحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ithm is any sin that incurs recompense; listing it after indecency broadens the prohibition beyond the gravest offenses.
rows.anchor: مطلق الذنب الذي يوجب الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghy is unjustly exalting oneself over another; “without right” clarifies its technical sense because the root can mean any seeking.
rows.anchor: وهو الاستعلاء على الغير ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification may exclude rightfully prevailing against an aggressor; if that is also called baghy, the shared term deters it and encourages pardon. Alternatively, the qualification stresses that baghy is inherently without right.
rows.anchor: من تعاطيه وندبا إلى العفو كما تقدم مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing called a divine partner has any revealed warrant; the verse teaches that religious fundamentals require decisive proof, especially monotheism.
rows.anchor: إرشادا إلى أن أصول الدين لا يجوز أعتمادها إلا بقاطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also forbids people to claim what they do not know about Him, whether the claim concerns fundamentals or other matters and whether specific or inferred from general knowledge.
rows.anchor: ما ليس لكم به علم بخصوصه ولا هو مستند إلى علم أعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community has a fixed term; God does not hasten its end because He fears loss or harm, and any opposition ultimately harms only its people.
rows.anchor: ولهم أجل لا بد من استيفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hour means the shortest conceivable time in ordinary speech, and no community can delay or advance its appointed term.
rows.anchor: لأنها أقل الأوقات في الاستعمال في العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause may attach to the whole conditional or to the fixed term, which God set with full knowledge and without acquiring new knowledge.
rows.anchor: لأن الذي ضربه لهم ما ضربه إلا وهو عالم بكل ما يكون من أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause links to 7:24: humanity will multiply into communities, each with its own term rather than being destroyed collectively at one time.
rows.anchor: وتكون الآية معلمة بأنهم ستناسلون فيكثرون حتى يكونوا أمما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an challenges those who claimed they could produce its like: if sincere, they would have done so, even after claiming it was not uniquely true.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لو كانوا صادقين في دعواهم لقالوا مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to whistling and clapping shows that self-proclaimed masters of eloquence could not answer the Qur'an's height and descended to animal noises.
rows.anchor: نزلتم إلى أصوات الحيوانات العجم حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they could rival the Qur'an through speech, they would not substitute costly spending, bodily suffering, and death for that challenge, with eternal disgrace as the result.
rows.anchor: لو قدرتم في معارضته على إنفاق الأقوال لما عدلتم عنه إلى إنفاق الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathering of disbelievers distinguishes wicked people from good ones: this is just toward disbelievers and a favor to believers.
rows.anchor: عدلا في الكافرين وفضلا عاى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wicked are heaped together, with the repetition clarifying a real piling and tight joining like piled clouds, before being cast into Hell, a place of distress and confinement.
rows.anchor: جمع الشيء بعضه فوق بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They alone are the losers because their loss is complete: at the gathering they bought their own destruction with their wealth.
rows.anchor: لأنهم اشتروا بأموالهم إهلاك أنفسهم بذلك الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past-tense labels for disbelievers could despairingly include those who later repent; God therefore tells the Prophet to invite them to stop, promising forgiveness and erasure of past sins.
rows.anchor: أقبل توبة من تاب منهم بمجرد انتهائه عن حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording of forgiveness emphasizes the benefit itself: past sins are erased in both substance and trace, with no punishment or reproach.
rows.anchor: بناه للمفعول لأن النافع نفس الغفران وهو محو الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they persist and resume hostilities, the precedent of earlier peoples has already run its course, as shown by reports of the past and what was witnessed at Badr.
rows.anchor: أي وجدت وانقضت ونفذت فلا مرد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's purpose is to oppose those who turned from the previous surah's call to God's oneness and obedience, and to support those who turn to Him.
rows.anchor: مقصودها معاداة من أعرض عما دعت إليه السورة الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest evidence is the story of the three left behind at Tabuk: their admitted, unjustified absence could suggest inward rejection, so they were shunned in every way, even in speech.
rows.anchor: فصة المحلفين فإنهم - لاعترافهم بالتخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name al-Tawbah reflects their repentance; their disavowal and social exclusion caused that repentance, so the effect is named for its cause.
rows.anchor: لأن البراءة منهم 0 بهجرانهم حتى رد السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barā'a suits the surah's stated purpose; al-Fāḍiḥa suits its exposure of those worthy of disavowal, and al-Buḥūth its searching into a hated person's condition.
rows.anchor: وتسميتها براءة واضح أيضا فيما ذكر من مقصودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lists further names meaning scattering, repelling, exposing, disgracing, destroying, driving away, and chastising, since the surah uncovers and separates blameworthy states.
rows.anchor: والمبعثرة هو المنفرة والمثبرة والحفارة والمخزية والمهلكة والمشردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Musharrida especially fits the surah's subject and echoes 8:57, “drive them away,” by describing its dispersing force.
rows.anchor: المشردة عظيمة المناسبة مع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The titles surah al-Athab and al-Muqashqisha also suit it; al-Muqashqisha is said to mean clearing one of hypocrisy, like sores peeling as they heal.
rows.anchor: إن معناه المبرئة من النمفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who knows that God, His Messenger, and believers disown a person for an act should turn away from that act.
rows.anchor: من عرف أن الله برئ منه ورسوله والمؤمنون لأمر فهو جدير بأن يرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also derives al-Muqashqisha from a reduplicated root of gathering: the surah gathers the kinds and conditions of hypocrites; gathering and separation are linked because each presupposes the other.
rows.anchor: وعندي أيضا أنه مضاعف القش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexeme qash and its related form iqshash can refer to foraging and gathering food from here and there.
rows.anchor: والقش والإقشاش : طلب المأكول من ها هنا وها هنا لجمعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word qishsha for a monkey is linked to gathering edible things it sees into its mouth.
rows.anchor: القردة كأنها لجمعها ما رأت مما يؤكل في فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other examples include a small monkey or child, beetle-like bug, scavenger, snake-skin sound, and a camel recovering from mange; the author derives them from compactness, gathering, or separation in healing.
rows.anchor: تقششت القروح وتقشقشت - إذا تقشرت للبرء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase qashshah bi-kalam means that he hurt people with vile speech, gathering their worries against him or gathering their faults.
rows.anchor: إذا تكلم بقبيح الكلام وآذاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qash can mean gathering an object by hand until it flakes, moving like a gaunt person, eating scraps, dried vegetation ready to collect, inferior dates, or a large bucket that gathers much.
rows.anchor: قش الشيء : جمعه بيده حتى يتحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas the two al-Muqashqishatan, clearing shirk; another report recommends al-Kafirun before sleep as immunity from shirk, and the author says they clear subtle or manifest association and hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: عند منامك فإنها براءة من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qashqasha can describe the sound before a camel's full roar, whose swelling beginning gathers force.
rows.anchor: والقشقشة يحكى بها الصوت قبل الهدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qashqasha is also a stick, either because it gathers what it is used for or because its bark is peeled like snake skin.
rows.anchor: أو لأنها يقشر عنها لحاؤها كما يقشر جلد الحية

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says a ṣadʿ may crack only on one face without passing through, whereas a shaqq must split all the way through.
rows.anchor: الصدع ربما كان في أحد الوجهين غير نافذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversed root sh-q-q supplies separation examples: a camel's tooth emerging splits flesh, dividing a staff separates a group, and hardship splits or burdens a person.
rows.anchor: فرق باثنيتين وفرق بين الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further examples include the dying person's fixed gaze separating from other directions, the dawn dividing darkness, and a straight lightning path splitting a cloud.
rows.anchor: نظر إلى شيء لا يرتد إليه طرفه
